cultural_notes: Jackson Hole is a high mountain valley (a 'hole' in mountain-man usage) between the Gros Ventre and Teton ranges near the Idaho border; humans have been drawn here for more than 11,000 years (source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackson_Hole; nps.gov Grand Teton cultural history)

the valley was settled by homesteaders and ranchers facing poor soils, a short growing season, and limited market access -- log construction was near-universal given the absence of local sawmills; 'dude ranch vernacular' (log with board-and-batten additions) defines the historic building style (source: jacksonholehistory.org; wyoshpo.wyo.gov Teton County NRHP; en.wikipedia.org historical buildings of Grand Teton)

Teton Village and Jackson Hole Mountain Resort turned the valley into a year-round destination and drove the ski economy; the 1965 Alpenhof Lodge introduced Swiss-Alpine architecture to the village (source: wyoshpo.wyo.gov Teton County, Alpenhof Lodge)

the National Elk Refuge borders the town; elk-antler arches ring the Town Square -- a genuine wildlife-and-conservation civic identity (source: nps.gov Grand Teton; region knowledge -- verify exact framing before production)
